title: Problem-solving and social support appraisals in the cross-sectional association between social media integration and PCL-5 symptom severity
content:
by Tyrone B. Pretorius, Anita Padmanabhanunni

The present study investigated the relationship between social media integration and PTSD-consistent symptomatology among South African university students, with a specific focus on the roles of problem-solving appraisal and perceived social support. Participants were 491 students who completed the Social Media Use Integration Scale, the Problem-Solving Inventory-20, the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support, and the Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlations, and mediation and moderation analyses with PROCESS. Social media integration was positively associated with overall PTSD-consistent symptomatology and all symptom clusters measured by the PCL-5. Problem-solving appraisal was negatively associated with PCL-5 symptom severity. It partially mediated the relationship between social media integration and PCL-5 symptom severity. Perceived social support showed a more selective pattern of association, with higher support linked to lower negative alterations in cognition and mood, as well as hyperarousal. In addition, social support moderated the relationship between social media use and PCL-5 symptom severity, avoidance, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and hyperarousal. These findings suggest that greater social media integration is associated with higher PCL-5 symptom severity, whereas problem-solving appraisal and perceived social support serve as important protective factors. Interventions aimed at strengthening coping appraisals and supportive social networks may help reduce trauma-related distress among young adults in the context of frequent social media use.
author: Tyrone B. Pretorius
